items.content_html:
Summary

WebView Android doesn't expose the Device Posture API, so this sets webview_android to false for api.Navigator.devicePosture and api.DevicePosture (and its type and change_event) instead of mirroring Chrome.

Test results and supporting details

Chromium turns the API off for WebView in aw_field_trials.cc:

// Disable device posture API as the framework implementation causes
// AwContents to leak in apps that don't call destroy().
aw_feature_overrides.DisableFeature(blink::features::kDevicePosture);

That line landed in May 2024 (CL 5548161, crbug.com/335314107), before Chrome 132 shipped the API, so WebView never had it. This matches the test in #30973: 'devicePosture' in navigator is false in WebView 155 and true in Chrome on the same phone.

I left the device-posture media feature as it is, since #30973 shows it working in WebView.

The same Chromium change also turns off kViewportSegments, so api.Viewport.segments may have the same problem in WebView. I haven't tested that one.

Related issues

Fixes #30973
items.title: Mark the Device Posture API as unsupported in WebView Android

items.content_html:
Firefox 160 added support for the headers option of the WebTransport() constructor in https://bugzil.la/2081470.

It is the request-side companion to WebTransport.responseHeaders (https://bugzil.la/2033220), which #31022 added

This PR adds api.WebTransport.WebTransport.options_headers_parameter. In every engine the option shipped in the same change as responseHeaders, so the data matches that feature:

  • Chrome: 157. A single runtime flag, WebTransportHeaders, gates both members. It was made stable ("Enables WebTransportOptions.headers and WebTransport.responseHeaders by default") when chrome/VERSION was 157.
    Note, chromestatus says 156 https://chromestatus.com/feature/5194104408506368
  • Safari: preview. Both were added in the same WebKit commit. Safari iOS is false, the same as responseHeaders.

Related docs work can be tracked in

  • mdn/content#46279 and
  • mdn/content#46284
items.title: FF160 WebTransport() constructor headers option

items.content_html:
Firefox 160 added support for BYOB readers on WebTransport datagrams in https://bugzil.la/2007755. You opt in by passing the new datagramsReadableType: "bytes" option to the WebTransport() constructor (Gecko commit).

This PR:

  • Sets api.WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream.byob_readers to Firefox 160.
  • Adds api.WebTransport.WebTransport.options_datagramsReadableType_parameter. The values for other browsers come from their source:
    • Chrome: false. The option is in the IDL but behind the WebTransportDatagramsReadableType runtime flag, which is still experimental. Chrome's datagram readable stream has always been a byte stream, so its existing byob_readers data is unchanged.
    • Safari: preview. WebKit shipped this option as datagramsReadableMode in 26.4 and renamed it to datagramsReadableType in July 2026. The Safari 27.2 branch (safari-7625.2.8) still has the old name.
    • Deno: omitted, because Deno doesn't implement the option.
  • Fixes spec_url on api.WebTransport.byob_readers and api.WebTransport.createUnidirectionalStream.byob_readers. Both cover BYOB on streams, not datagrams, so they now point to #example-stream-byob instead of #example-datagrams-byob.

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46274
items.title: FF160 WebTransport BYOB datagram readers and datagramsReadableType option

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds web extension data for icon_variants and the related icon properties, and corrects menus.update.icons for Safari.

  • icon_variants as a manifest key and in action, browser_action and page_action: Safari 18.2. Chrome 127 for the manifest key and Chrome 136 for action, both behind --enable-features=ExtensionIconVariants.
  • variants in action.setIcon() and browserAction.setIcon(): Safari 18.2.
  • iconVariants in menus.create() and menus.update(): Safari 26.2, with the earlier icon_variants spelling as the alternative name from Safari 18.2.
  • The any size key for icons and default_icon: Safari 18.2.
  • menus.update.icons: Safari 18.

The mdn_url for icon_variants is left out until the MDN page exists.

Test results and supporting details

npm run lint -- webextensions passes.

items.content_html:
FF160 is supposed to add support for getStats() in WebTransportSendStream/ReceiveStream/SendGroup in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2021710 but Claude and tests show that it is not in, and is likely to be in 161.

This updates things to match the current state for all browsers prior to whenever this goes in.

Tests:

  • https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stream-stats.https.any.worker.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned
  • https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stream-stats.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned
  • https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stream-stats.https.any.html?label=master&label=stable
  • https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stream-stats.https.any.worker.html?label=master&label=stable

In fact WebTransportSendStream.getStats() and WebTransportReceiveStream.getStats() always reject with NotSupportedError and WebTransportSendGroup.getStats() always resolves with an empty object. This marks the original introductions as partial.

Safari: WebTransportSendGroup.getStats() counts only datagram bytes sent through the group, not stream bytes. Marked as partial_implementation.

Chrome: add impl_url links to the Chromium tracking issues. This is expected to release around 159 - see https://chromestatus.com/feature/5235261159112704

Related FF docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46277
items.title: WebTransport stream/send group getStats(): mark partial implementations

items.content_html:
Summary

Marks ruby-position: inter-character as unsupported in Chrome and removes the inaccurate prefixed-support note. Mirrored Chromium-based entries follow the existing data model.

Test results and supporting details

  • Chromium's current parser accepts over and under and rejects inter-character. The Chrome 84 property definitions list only before and after for the prefixed property.
  • Formatting and data lint passed on an isolated older repository snapshot with the same changed file. The unit tests passed with equivalent PowerShell environment variables; npm test itself stopped on Windows because its unit-test script uses Unix environment-variable syntax.
  • I did not run browser tests.

Prepared with Codex assistance.

Related issues

Fixes #30993.
items.title: Correct Chromium inter-character ruby support
